question: What does a drag on empty canvas select, and how does the box look?
look: a 3px rgb(0, 114, 240) outline just outside the rectangle from the start point to the pointer, no fill, drawn over the whole window. The blocks it touches get a thin outline, no handles and no toolbar; the section's chrome stays on screen
rule: a block the box touches is selected (case B touched only a corner of the paragraph and selected it); two or more selected blocks get the group toolbar (Stack Blocks, Align Group)
steps: pointer events on the frame document from an empty point below the paragraph; nothing was saved (Save stayed disabled, no undo needed)

measured2.how: real mouse input in headless Chrome, 2026-11-04. Nothing saved: Exit Without Saving after every run.

threshold.rule: the box starts once the pointer is 30px from the start

measured2.startsFrom: anywhere in the section: the grid, its margins, and the padding above and below the grid

acrossSections.box: keeps growing over the next section
acrossSections.rule: only blocks of the section it started in are selected
acrossSections.downIntoNext: box over a block of section 3, started in section 2: nothing selected
acrossSections.upIntoPrevious: box over the paragraph of section 2, started in section 3: the section 3 block it touches, not the paragraph

measured2.autoScroll: none: 3.4s of moves at 1px from the bottom and from the top edge, scroll position unchanged

live.nothingSelectedBefore: held selection follows the box: paragraph, then nothing, then heading and paragraph, then nothing; released on nothing: nothing selected

withASelection.boxOverShape: held: paragraph and shape; after release: shape only

measured2.escape: no effect while held: box and selection stay
notMeasured: a drag under 30px with a selection, then release: ours treats it as a click
a box with a selection that touched a block and then left it: ours goes back to the selection
the small type label a hovered block shows (TEXT) in the shot: ours has no such label
